answers with solutions
your question doesn't mention the part of the sentence where the second half of your sentence is missing:
"i am not in a XXXXX that has been previously visited."
to understand why your sentence can be accepted (and not rejected) you really need to understand that words like "new" or "newly" can be used at different XXXXXs within a sentence.
in english this is often used as a sort of "preposition", but in some other languages it can be used to modify something by pointing to a previous occurrence of the same thing, and not to imply an exact location or time. 
as such, in this case we are not going to use such words: we are going to use "been" or "been previously visited":

he was travelling in new countries.

"new" is an adverb:

he was travelling in new countries.

"other" is an adjective:

he was travelling in other countries.

and you already know what the meaning of "been" is:

i was
